title: (No AI) Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
content:
![A patent illustration depicting a man standing in a room with a large television screen displaying the home page of a streaming service.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/Screenshot-2026-11-25-at-11.34.07-AM.png?quality=90&strip=all&crop=2.859375,3.7218027238494,93.788122558594,91.658221639303)

Last year, [Google filed a patent](https://www.digitaltrends.com/movies/google-filed-a-patent-for-an-ai-channel-that-casts-you-as-the-lead/) for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users. The patent has been rejected, but unfortunately, Google might appeal or resubmit an amended version, and we could see this monstrosity come to market.

First [spotted by Patentlyze](https://patentlyze.com/patent/google-ai-made-tv-channel-built-around-you/), the patent - which was filed last May and published last week - describes how My Channel would use a person's demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that …

title: (No AI) FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
author: Emma Roth
content:
![SpaceX’s facility in California](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/05/gettyimages-2269580650.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

In [an announcement on Wednesday](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-427572A1.pdf), the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned [company's "Starmind" initiative](https://www.spacex.com/spacexsi/starmind). With [several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/845453/space-data-centers-astronomers), including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full "constellation" of AI satellites.

[The FCC's approval requires](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-1273A1.pdf) SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX's request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in [space "graveyard" orbits](https://www.nesdis.noaa.gov/news/graveyard-orbits-and-the-satellite-afterlife), rather than …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/science/1042278/spacex-fcc-starmind-ai-space-data-centers)
